title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — 10.2.1 Reading: Intensive Reading (Factual Texts)

PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

A factual text gives true information about a topic. In this sub-strand you will read factual texts of about 320 words on hygiene and sanitation, answer questions about them, work out the meaning of new words, and learn good reading habits that help you understand and remember what you read.

## Strand 10.0: Hygiene and Sanitation
Sub-strand 10.2.1: Reading: Intensive Reading (Factual Texts)
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension
b) apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information
c) realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information

## What this sub-strand covers
• Factual Texts

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should we read at the right speed?
2. What should we do to remember what we read?

## Core competencies
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner manipulates electronic devices to read factual information based on the theme of hygiene and sanitation.
• Learning to Learn: It is developed as the learner uses resource materials like the encyclopaedia to obtain relevant information.

## Values
• Respect: This is developed as the learner displays open mindedness to the factual information read from different sources.
• Unity: This is achieved as the learner shares resources amicably with other learners during the activities that require the use of electronic devices.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Personal Hygiene: It is enhanced as the learner reads stories on hygiene and watches a video on how to take care of oneself by focusing on personal hygiene and sanitation.

## Links to other learning areas
• The learner applies the knowledge of reading for factual information to all other areas of learning as they require this skill.
• The learner also uses the skills gained in using the dictionary and other reference materials to other learning areas like Kiswahili which require them to use dictionaries as well.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 English Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Theme 10.0 Hygiene and Sanitation, Sub-strand 10.2.1 Intensive Reading: Factual Texts

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Reading a factual text: Germs and clean hands

LESSON 1: READING A FACTUAL TEXT: GERMS AND CLEAN HANDS
=======================================================

## What you will learn
• Read a factual text of about 320 words on hygiene.
• Answer factual and inferential questions on the text.
• Work out the meaning of new words from the text.

Curriculum outcomes: a) read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension

## Introduction
Every day your hands touch doors, desks, balls, money and food. Can you see what they pick up? Read the text below to find out why washing your hands is one of the simplest ways to stay healthy.

## Notes
### What is a factual text?
A factual text tells us true things about the world. It does not tell a made-up story. It often has a title, short paragraphs, and sometimes headings or a list of steps.

### Read the text
**Germs and Clean Hands**

Germs are tiny living things. They are so small that we cannot see them without a microscope. Some germs are harmless, but others cause diseases such as diarrhoea, cholera and colds.

Germs spread easily. When a person uses the toilet or latrine, germs from faeces can stay on their hands. If that person then touches food, a cup or another person's hand without washing, the germs move on. Flies also carry germs. A fly that lands on waste and then on uncovered food leaves germs behind.

The good news is that we can stop many germs. Washing hands with soap and clean water removes germs that plain water leaves behind. Soap loosens the dirt and oil on the skin, and rinsing carries the germs away.

To wash your hands well, wet them with clean running water. Rub soap on both hands. Scrub the palms, the backs of the hands, between the fingers and under the nails for about twenty seconds. Rinse well and dry your hands with a clean cloth or let them dry in the air. At school you can use a tap or a leaky tin that pours water slowly.

When should you wash your hands? Always wash them after using the toilet, before eating, before handling food, after touching rubbish and after playing outside. Wash them after blowing your nose or coughing into them.

Other simple habits also keep germs away. Cover food and drinking water. Boil or treat drinking water when you are not sure it is safe. Keep toilets and latrines clean and cover the hole of a pit latrine. Throw refuse in a bin or a rubbish pit.

Clean hands protect you, your family and your classmates. Hygiene is everyone's responsibility.

### Working out new words
If you meet a new word, read the sentences around it. For example, "Soap loosens the dirt... and rinsing carries the germs away" helps you guess that rinsing means washing off with water.

## Key words
• germs — tiny living things that can cause disease
• microscope — an instrument that makes very small things look bigger
• faeces — solid waste that passes out of the body
• refuse — rubbish or waste (said REF-yoos)

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Factual question: Name two diseases caused by germs mentioned in the text.

Answer: Any two of diarrhoea, cholera and colds.

### Example 2
Inferential question: Why do you think the writer says hygiene is everyone's responsibility?

Answer: Because germs spread from one person to another, so if one person is careless others can get sick too.

## Activity: Read, find and act
You will need: Copy of the text or a digital device with the text, Soap, water and a basin or leaky tin
1. Read the text silently once, then read it again with a partner, taking turns paragraph by paragraph.
2. Underline three words you did not know and guess their meaning from the sentences around them.
3. Answer the practice questions in your exercise book.
4. In groups, role play the handwashing steps from the text while one learner reads them aloud.

## Practice
1. Why can't we see germs?
2. How do flies spread germs?
3. List four times when you should wash your hands.
4. What does the word scrub mean in the text?

## Summary
• A factual text gives true information.
• Germs spread through dirty hands, flies, food and water.
• Washing hands with soap and clean water removes germs.

### Answers to practice
1. They are too small to see without a microscope.
2. They land on waste and then on uncovered food, leaving germs behind.
3. Any four: after using the toilet, before eating, before handling food, after touching rubbish, after playing outside, after blowing your nose.
4. To rub hard to clean.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Good reading habits

LESSON 2: GOOD READING HABITS
=============================

## What you will learn
• Read at the right speed without pointing or murmuring.
• Use steps that help you remember what you read.
• Use an encyclopaedia or dictionary to find more information.

Curriculum outcomes: b) apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information

## Introduction
Two learners read the same text. One reads every word slowly with a finger and forgets the beginning by the end. The other reads smoothly and can tell you the main points. The difference is their reading habits.

## Notes
Reading habits are the ways we usually read. Good habits help us read faster and understand more.

### Before reading
- Sit upright in good light, with the book about 30 centimetres from your eyes.
- Look at the title, headings and pictures. Ask yourself: What will this text tell me?

### While reading
- Read in groups of words, not one word at a time. "Wash your hands / with soap / and clean water" is easier to understand than stopping at every word.
- Do not point at each word with your finger or a pencil, and do not move your lips when reading silently. These habits slow you down.
- Read at the right speed. Too fast and you miss facts; too slow and you lose the meaning. Slow down a little for difficult parts.
- If a word is new, guess its meaning from the sentence, then check it in a dictionary.

### After reading
- Say the main idea of each paragraph in your own words.
- Write down key facts as short notes.
- Answer questions, then go back to the text to check your answers.

### Finding more information
An encyclopaedia is a book or website with factual articles on many topics, arranged from A to Z. To learn more about cholera, look under the letter C. A dictionary gives the meaning and pronunciation of words. Both are useful when a factual text leaves you with questions.

### Why remember what we read?
We read factual texts to learn. If you remember that cholera spreads through dirty water and food, you will know to boil water and cover food. Reading carefully helps you make good choices.

## Key words
• reading habit — the usual way a person reads
• encyclopaedia — a book or website with facts on many topics arranged in alphabetical order
• main idea — the most important point of a paragraph or text

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Split this sentence into word groups for smooth reading: Cover your food to keep flies away from it.

Answer: Cover your food / to keep flies away / from it.

### Example 2
Under which letter would you look in an encyclopaedia to read about sanitation?

Answer: S

## Activity: Reading habits check
You will need: The text Germs and Clean Hands, Encyclopaedia or dictionary, or a digital device
1. In pairs, one learner reads a paragraph silently while the partner watches for pointing or lip movement.
2. Swap roles and give each other one tip to improve.
3. Write the main idea of each paragraph in one sentence.
4. Look up cholera or diarrhoea in an encyclopaedia or dictionary and share one new fact with the class.
5. Watch a short video on handwashing if available and pick out two steps it shows.

## Practice
1. Name two bad reading habits that slow you down.
2. What should you do before you start reading a text?
3. How can you check the meaning of a new word after guessing it?

## Summary
• Preview, read in word groups and review.
• Avoid pointing and murmuring when reading silently.
• Use an encyclopaedia or dictionary to learn more.

### Answers to practice
1. Pointing at words, moving your lips while reading silently (also reading word by word).
2. Look at the title, headings and pictures and think about what the text is about.
3. Look it up in a dictionary.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Why we read for information: Keeping toilets and latrines clean

LESSON 3: WHY WE READ FOR INFORMATION: KEEPING TOILETS AND LATRINES CLEAN
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Read a second factual text using good reading habits.
• Answer factual and inferential questions.
• Explain why reading for information is important.

Curriculum outcomes: a) read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension; b) apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information; c) realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information

## Introduction
A clean toilet protects the whole school. Read this factual text about sanitation and use the reading habits you learnt in the last lesson.

## Notes
### Read the text
**A Clean Toilet for Everyone**

Sanitation means the safe handling of human waste and refuse. Toilets and latrines are important parts of sanitation because they keep faeces away from people, food and water.

A flush toilet uses water to carry waste away through pipes. After using it, press the handle or pull the chain so that the waste is flushed. If there is no running water, pour water from a bucket into the bowl.

A pit latrine is a deep hole covered with a floor called a slab. Waste falls into the pit. A latrine must be kept covered with a lid when not in use so that flies cannot get in and out. Flies that visit uncovered latrines can carry germs to our food.

Everyone can help keep toilets clean. Aim well so that the floor stays dry. Use toilet paper and put it in the toilet or the pit, not on the floor. Never throw stones, bottles or plastic into a toilet or latrine, because they block it. Wash your hands with soap and water as soon as you leave.

People on duty should sweep and scrub the floor, rinse it with water and wipe the door handles. Many schools use a disinfectant to kill germs. Drainage around the toilet should be clear so that dirty water does not collect.

Dirty toilets smell bad and spread infection. When they are clean, learners are safe and comfortable. A clean toilet is a sign of a caring school.

### Reading for information
Why did we read this text carefully? Because it tells us what to do. A learner who has read it knows how to use a latrine safely and why the lid matters. Reading for information:

- helps us understand how things work;
- teaches us how to protect our health;
- helps us answer questions in all subjects;
- lets us share correct facts with our family.

Reading for comprehension means reading until you truly understand, not just saying the words.

## Key words
• latrine — a toilet built over a deep hole in the ground
• slab — the flat floor covering a pit latrine
• disinfectant — a liquid that kills germs
• drainage — the way water flows away from a place

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Factual: Why should a pit latrine be covered?

Answer: So that flies cannot get in and out and carry germs to food.

### Example 2
Inferential: Why does the writer say a clean toilet is a sign of a caring school?

Answer: Because keeping it clean shows people care about each other's health and comfort.

## Activity: Toilet duty role play
You will need: The text A Clean Toilet for Everyone, Broom, mop, bucket (for demonstration)
1. Read the text silently, then answer the practice questions.
2. In groups, role play a toilet duty team explaining to younger learners how to use and keep the latrine clean.
3. Discuss in your group: How did reading this text help you? Share your answer with the class.

## Practice
1. How does a flush toilet remove waste?
2. Name two things that should never be thrown into a toilet.
3. What does drainage mean in the text?
4. Give one reason why reading for information is important.

## Summary
• Toilets and latrines keep faeces away from people, food and water.
• Keep latrines covered and toilets clean and dry.
• Reading for information helps us understand and act wisely.

### Answers to practice
1. It uses water to carry waste away through pipes.
2. Any two: stones, bottles, plastic.
3. The way dirty water flows away so that it does not collect.
4. It teaches us how to protect our health (or helps us understand how things work, answer questions, share correct facts).
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 10.2.1 READING: INTENSIVE READING (FACTUAL TEXTS)
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. What is a factual text?
   A. A made-up story
   B. A text that gives true information
   C. A song
   D. A riddle

2. According to Germs and Clean Hands, what removes germs that plain water leaves behind?
   A. Sand
   B. Soap and clean water
   C. A towel
   D. Sunlight

3. For about how long should you scrub your hands?
   A. Two seconds
   B. Twenty seconds
   C. Two minutes
   D. Twenty minutes

4. In A Clean Toilet for Everyone, what is the floor that covers a pit latrine called?
   A. A lid
   B. A slab
   C. A drain
   D. A bowl

5. Why should we not throw plastic into a latrine?

6. Which is a good reading habit?
   A. Pointing at every word
   B. Moving your lips when reading silently
   C. Reading in groups of words
   D. Reading in poor light

7. What should you do after reading a text to remember it?
   A. Close the book and forget it
   B. Say the main ideas in your own words
   C. Read only the title
   D. Tear out the page

8. Where would you look to find more facts about cholera?
   A. A storybook
   B. An encyclopaedia
   C. A song book
   D. A diary

9. Why is it important to read for comprehension?

10. Which is NOT a reason for reading factual texts?
   A. To learn how things work
   B. To protect our health
   C. To share correct facts
   D. To make up stories
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 10.2.1 READING: INTENSIVE READING (FACTUAL TEXTS)
========================================

1. B. A text that gives true information
   Factual texts give true information.

2. B. Soap and clean water
   The text says soap and clean water remove germs.

3. B. Twenty seconds
   The text says about twenty seconds.

4. B. A slab
   The text calls it a slab.

5. It blocks the toilet or latrine.
   The text says stones, bottles and plastic block it.

6. C. Reading in groups of words
   Reading in word groups is faster and helps understanding.

7. B. Say the main ideas in your own words
   Retelling main ideas helps memory.

8. B. An encyclopaedia
   An encyclopaedia has factual articles on many topics.

9. So that we truly understand the information and can use it, for example to protect our health.
   Understanding helps us act on what we read.

10. D. To make up stories
   Factual texts are for true information, not made-up stories.

4. It teaches us how to protect our health (or helps us understand how things work, answer questions, share correct facts).

questions.question: What is a factual text?
options: A text that gives true information

questions.question: According to Germs and Clean Hands, what removes germs that plain water leaves behind?
questions.explanation: The text says soap and clean water remove germs.

questions.question: For about how long should you scrub your hands?
questions.explanation: The text says about twenty seconds.

questions.question: In A Clean Toilet for Everyone, what is the floor that covers a pit latrine called?
questions.explanation: The text calls it a slab.

questions.question: Why should we not throw plastic into a latrine?
questions.answer: It blocks the toilet or latrine.
questions.explanation: The text says stones, bottles and plastic block it.

questions.question: Which is a good reading habit?
options: Moving your lips when reading silently
questions.explanation: Reading in word groups is faster and helps understanding.

questions.question: What should you do after reading a text to remember it?
options: Close the book and forget it
Say the main ideas in your own words

questions.question: Where would you look to find more facts about cholera?
questions.explanation: An encyclopaedia has factual articles on many topics.

questions.question: Why is it important to read for comprehension?
questions.answer: So that we truly understand the information and can use it, for example to protect our health.
questions.explanation: Understanding helps us act on what we read.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason for reading factual texts?
questions.explanation: Factual texts are for true information, not made-up stories.
